conceptZh: 要：想要、需要；一隻手特別長的玩具機器人伸長手去拿，最後得到想要的東西。
object: a boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts with one very long arm, reaching for a gigantic lollipop on a high shelf and a tiny teaspoon
morph: a giant lollipop and a tiny spoon force the robot to improvise, and his reaching arm swings the pieces into the glyph 要
creativeAngle: 玩具機器人一隻手特別長，想要的糖果大得離譜、湯匙卻小得可憐，他到處亂想辦法，伸手一撈剛好撈出要字。
promptEn: An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale lemon-cream backdrop. Cast: one boxy toy robot built from mismatched parts, a square red body, a round blue head, a tiny yellow foot and one arm much longer than the other, plus one comically oversized swirly lollipop taller than he is. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 要, drawn in saturated tomato-red strokes, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with margins. 0.0-1.5s: the robot clanks in, spots a giant swirl lollipop leaning against the wall, and holds up his short arm to point; the lollipop is far too big for his hand and he stands on tiptoe, wobbling. The first narrated 要 lands as he stretches his long arm out in a happy reaching pose and a red stroke flies from his fingertips. 1.5-3.5s: he tries to lift the lollipop with a tiny teaspoon, which flicks the candy into a spin; he tries tugging it with the long arm, which stretches like a spring and snaps back, knocking his own head sideways with a clank. The second narrated 要 lands as the lollipop's swirl unspools into the strokes and clicks into place, completing 要 in the center. 3.5-5.0s: the robot, delighted, hugs the giant lollipop, which pulls him off the ground, and he squeaks into the air with his long arm stretched, then pops down onto his one tiny foot. As the word 我要 is spoken the robot points to his own chest with the short arm and then to the lollipop with the long arm, nodding vigorously. 5.0-8.0s: the glyph is perfectly still and readable for the last 3 seconds while the robot licks the lollipop at a distance with his long arm, bounces on his tiny foot, and his head spins once with happiness, away from the strokes. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin, clear tones, no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 要、要、我要 (ㄧㄠˋ、ㄧㄠˋ、ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ). The character twice with a short pause, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only. No background music, no extra speech, no subtitles or flashing effects; stylized toy characters only, no real people.

conceptZh: 要：想要。積木小隊想要架子上的大餅乾，疊成高塔去拿卻被小老鼠一戳就倒，整隊縮成一顆方塊球滿場彈跳，每撞一下就敲出一筆，最後穩穩坐在「要」字上，拍胸口伸手說「我要」。
object: a squad of chunky interlocking toy building bricks that march in a line, stack into a wobbly tower, and fall as one tight bouncing cube
morph: the toppled brick squad ricochets around the frame as a rubbery cube; each clack against floor, wall, ceiling and the mouse's head knocks one red stroke into place until 要 stands complete, 覀 on top and 女 beneath
creativeAngle: 全新彈跳鏈概念，捨棄舊版機器人伸長手的設定：改由積木小隊「疊高塔→被戳倒→變彈跳方塊」三段式物理笑點，每一下撞擊都敲出一筆，「想要」的目標（餅乾）從頭到尾可見，詞語「我要」用拍胸口加伸手的動作同步演出。
promptEn:
An 8-second bright, clean toy-animation clip on a solid pale butter-yellow backdrop, nothing busy behind. Cast: a squad of six chunky interlocking toy building bricks in blue, green, orange and white, each with two dot eyes and little stub feet, marching in a strict line like proud little soldiers; one tiny cheeky cartoon mouse with big round ears and a permanent grin, an original design; and one giant golden cookie sitting on a high shelf at upper right. The only text on screen is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 要, built from saturated tomato-red strokes with the component 覀 on top and 女 beneath, ending centered, uncropped, about 70 percent of frame height with clear margins.

0.0-1.5s: the brick squad marches in from the left, halts with a crisp stomp, and all six pairs of eyes swing up to the cookie on the shelf. The front brick points at it with a stub arm, and the whole line leans forward with hungry stares. The mouse pops up beside the cookie, taps it, and grins down at them.

1.5-3.5s: the squad charges the shelf and clacks together into a tall wobbling tower, brick on brick, the top one straining toward the cookie with the first narrated 要 landing on that reach. The tower sways left, sways right. The mouse zips down the wall in a blur, pokes the bottom brick with one finger, and zips back up. The tower tips in slow motion for a frozen half-beat, every brick wide-eyed.

3.5-5.5s: the tower slams to the floor with a big squashy BONK and snaps together into one tight rubbery cube that springs straight back up. It ricochets wildly: floor CLACK, left wall CLACK, ceiling CLACK, a soft boing off the mouse's head that leaves the mouse cross-eyed and giggling, floor again. Each hit knocks one red stroke into the center of the frame, and the second narrated 要 lands as the final strokes snap in and 要 stands complete and perfectly formed.

5.5-8.0s: the glyph holds perfectly still and fully readable for the last 2.5 seconds plus the tail of the previous beat, no stroke ever covered. The cube's last bounce drops it gently onto the very top edge of the glyph's top horizontal stroke, where it pops apart back into six small bricks sitting in a proud row, small enough that every stroke stays visible. As the word 我要 is spoken, the front brick pats its own chest and then stretches both stub arms toward the cookie with a big nod. The mouse, charmed, shoves the cookie off the shelf; it tumbles down and the bricks catch it together, wobble, and give a tiny victory bounce, all away from the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice speaks slowly and distinctly in clear Taiwanese Mandarin with clear tones and no erhua, reading exactly these syllables: 要、要、我要 (ㄧㄠˋ、ㄧㄠˋ、ㄨㄛˇ ㄧㄠˋ). The character twice with a short pause between, then the word once, then stop. The word is audio only; no vocabulary text, subtitles or other text appear. Soft cartoon clack and boing sounds only, no background music louder than the voice, no extra speech, no flashing effects, no watermark. Stylized toy bricks and a cartoon mouse only; no real people or realistic human figures.
